speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This social compact among Singaporeans forms the bedrock that has enabled us to overcome many challenges faced in nation-building over the years.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our unity and strength in diversity is a unique part of our social fabric that is vital to the survival and progress of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Recently, the COVID-19 pandemic crisis brought out the very best of our Singapore community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We have seen the bravery and sacrifices of our frontline teams and heard of anecdotal stories of neighbours and friends within communities caring for and reaching out to one another in these challenging times.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But, Sir, on the other hand, as a result of the pandemic, we have also observed the polarisation of some societies along the lines of socio-economic status, race and nationality.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Some of the incidents gained widespread publicity, amplified through social media and other online platforms.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Such issues are highly emotive in nature and can easily serve to divide us, if not carefully managed.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is a timely reminder that we cannot take social harmony in Singapore for granted.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It can also prompt a deeper reflection about our values and what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must, however, exercise ample deliberation in managing the discourse.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must remember that we did not build the social compact we have where we enjoy racial and religious harmony overnight and it, certainly, did not happen by chance.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It took generations of effort, understanding, compromise and reaching out to grow the common spaces we share in order to attain what we have.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is a precious commodity that we must not freely give up.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the TODAY Youth Survey published in November last year, it is clear that our youths are progressively seized with and are inclined to speak their minds on issues such as race and religion.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our demographic is also slowly moving in a different direction.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: With this trend, it will mean that there will be a whole segment of the next generation of Singaporeans born of these marriages who will also join in the discussions of race and religion but from a wholly different perspective.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We are, therefore, likely to grow into a more diverse society in the future.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   Since the M3 network was established some years ago, we are now in a better position to understand how our outreach efforts can be coordinated to enhance our community.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Organisations and agencies have adopted a collaborative attitude to achieve better outcomes for the people.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there are still residents in rental units facing multigenerational issues, and this hinders their aspirations to achieve a better life.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we coordinate and work more closely with Malay/Muslim organisations that are actively helping the residents in order to avoid duplication of efforts?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   In Cheng San-Seletar, my team of volunteers run a research project to better understand the needs of families which have an incarcerated family member.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More often than not, these offenders are the sole breadwinner, like the father, husband or son.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Incarceration is something that can impact the institution of family.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although the offender was the one being incarcerated, his family members are also affected.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Usually, the assistance or support given to the offender's family only comes at the beginning or the end of the offender's sentence.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If we look at it, usually at the beginning of the offender's sentence, the offender's family may not feel desperate for daily needs.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, as time goes by, the offenders' families may feel trapped and depressed.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If we are not careful, other family members can be affected, too.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Efforts, such as reintegration support for offenders and families should be stepped up.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can FITRAH monitor and identify any multigenerational problems in the family, and how does FITRAH help those families?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to coordinate efforts and assistance for the family, not only at the beginning or the end of the prison sentence, but also for the entire incarceration period, so that the families of the offenders are not neglected?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More families are facing complex issues such as mental health and teenage pregnancies, and there is a need for FITRAH to mobilise volunteers to help these families.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, how can the FITRAH structure be strengthened for the long term so that this effort can continue?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   When I was given the opportunity to serve in MENDAKI's Committee on The Future Economy, we surveyed our students to understand how we can support their aspirations and ensure that they have a place and role in the future economy.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When asked where they received career advice, students from madrasahs and secular schools shared that they usually asked their parents and relatives, although schools now have education and career counsellors.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While family advice is important, our young people in this generation are growing up in a different era and economy where job and education opportunities are very much different, compared to 20 years ago.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Apart from preparing students with skills even while they are still school, how can MENDAKI work with companies and industries to support the transition to new growth areas?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   Boosting social mobility and uplifting the success of our community do not come from policy changes alone.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It requires a lot of hard work to build a supportive culture – providing access to networks, advisors or mentors and peer support to help our young people make the right choices in life.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Can the Government give an update on the M3 youth mentoring programmes and the value derived from these programmes in the eyes of the mentees?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: What is the demand for these mentoring programmes and how much of the demand is being fulfilled?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How quickly can the programmes be extended to ITE and Polytechnic students?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   The number of Malay families living in rental housing cited in the latest population survey is something that has been noted.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: At the same time, we know that many families in public rental flats aspire to become homeowners.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, over the past decade, the Malay/Muslim community has achieved much progress in both secular and religious fields.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We should be proud that the Malay community, through its awareness, determination, drive, effort and hard work, has managed to excel.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: During this period, we have seen many more young Malay/Muslims excelling in higher education.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, to achieve further success, we have to look at the gaps and challenges before us and try to find solutions for each one.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The Malay community is known for its "gotong royong" spirit.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Nonetheless, as the world is changing rapidly, we also need to learn from others to gain new knowledge and skills to overcome the current challenges.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As the Malay proverb goes, whenever it floods, the shoreline changes shape, that is, when a major change takes place, everything else will change, too.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: So, while many people may be happy to just swim in a small pond, the Malay community now aspires to swim in the ocean.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, there is also another proverb cautioning us that if our fishing line is short, do not test the ocean, that is, if we do not have the capacity, do not attempt something beyond our capabilities.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A rapidly changing world has impacted on our stability and traditional sources of income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Careers that used to provide stable employment are now facing challenges and becoming scarce.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These careers have been replaced by new forms of jobs that change quickly and this requires us to be nimble and adaptable to ensure a stable income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Our workforce is challenged by stiff competition from foreign workers flooding into our country, hungry for job opportunities that are increasingly becoming scarce in their own countries.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, in terms of monthly income, the Malay community is lagging behind.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Organisations tasked to address this challenge must ensure that they have made appropriate and sufficient preparations.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: First, by identifying jobs that will provide the most opportunities for our community right now and in the future.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, by identifying the community's inclinations and strengths, so that any necessary preparations and adaptations can take place now in order to prepare us for a work environment that has changed and will change in the future.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: All this will certainly influence the focus of our education in the future.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A focus on education that prepares our children in navigating future challenges must be emphasised.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Forward-thinking education should be the basis of their curriculum and any exposure that they have to undergo should be future-realistic.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We also need to find new ways to help Malay students excel in innovation and creativity, in Islamic finance which is being increasingly accepted in the global market including fintech, pharmaceuticals, robotics with its sophisticated use of nanotechnology and green technology, which are the bases of the new and future economy.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: For these new fields, we also need the expertise of religious scholars to enlighten the community on matters that require our involvement.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As such, I would like to ask the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs the following questions.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope that the Minister and MENDAKI will share these plans, so that the Malay community knows the direction they need to take in this rapidly-changing world.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would also like to ask what are MUIS' plans to equip our asatizahs with the knowledge and expertise in the areas of fintech, pharmaceuticals, robotics and green technology?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The community needs to know if there are any asatizahs in leadership who are knowledgeable in these fields and, at the same time, able to delve deeper into Islamic jurisprudence and syariah issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would also like to know how the Malay community can learn from the current asatizahs who are experts on these issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, our young Malays are increasingly getting excellent results in the "O" and "A" Level examinations, as well as in their studies at the local Universities.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These include madrasah students who obtained distinctions despite being burdened with a much higher number of subjects compared to their peers in secular schools.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This shows that there are young Malays with huge potential who need to be given the full attention, assistance and support.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Besides the increase in the number of Malay students in local Universities, there is also a growing number of young Malays who are furthering their studies at the Bachelor's degree or postgraduate level in foreign universities.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is to ensure that our Malay students' ambitions and aspirations are not hindered due to financial matters.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In this regard, I have some questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, what is the average loan amount given out by MENDAKI every year?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Going forward, the Malay community would like to know clearly whether there is a masterplan by MENDAKI to propel the Malay community forward, in line with the demands of IR 4.0.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I shared my views on how we can further strengthen efforts to continue our progress by expanding educational fields and knowledge to keep up with the changing times.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Before I end my speech, I would like to touch on current developments that we must pay attention to, especially by Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It also depends on efforts to do good and, at the same time, endeavours to help Muslims follow Islamic values more closely.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, please take your two cuts together, please.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, in last year's Committee of Supply debates, I asked about the KelasMateMatika, or KMM, programme and I was pleased that KMM had successfully prepared students for primary school.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am also excited about the School Readiness Class (KSS) programme announced last year.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: KMM and KSS are effective because they are not only meant for our children, but their parents as well.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: A KMM participant in Chua Chu Kang told me that the programme gives her confidence when teaching Mathematics to her child.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is encouraging because many parents participating in the programme come from low-income families and may not be highly educated.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Educational assistance is not just for children, but also for parents in their lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, what are the efforts to improve lifelong learning for young couples and workers in our community?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   The Singapore Community Wakaf (WMS) was announced in 2020 to generate a sustainable income to support the long-term needs of our community which includes religious institutions, asatizah development and community programmes.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: An Advisory Panel has been set up to review the necessary steps for the wakaf.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And this includes considering proposed amendments to existing laws.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, I agree that we need to restore the spirit and culture of endowing property for the benefit of society and nation, as those before us had done in the past, which helped established many of our religious institutions and welfare bodies through wakaf.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To achieve this objective, I had proposed in my previous Parliamentary speech that we need to establish a holistic ecosystem, including a more comprehensive dispute resolution framework and a public awareness campaign, on estate planning.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our community needs to be prepared for a rainy day.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Government also consider setting up a dedicated department in the Syariah Court or MUIS to hear any disputes related to the issue of Muslim inheritance, including wakaf?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   Wakaf is a voluntary charitable endowment made in the form of cash or property.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It is made by Muslims for religious purposes and allows the perpetual use of the asset for charity.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It is an important source of funds to supplement how the community can fulfil and support its community and religious needs.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: As such, I would also like to know what MUIS' efforts are in educating the public regarding wakaf and whether input is being sought from the community on how the wakaf assets are being used.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This is because I believe that, by doing so, it would put the Muslim community's mind at ease and may encourage the community to contribute further to the fund.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, may I know what are MUIS' plans to grow and invest the fund?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Minister also consider introducing a similar concept for the rest of society to consider endowing their assets to charitable perpetual uses?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   It can be difficult for families in need to navigate the social support systems to get timely and holistic help or to gain access to national initiatives that may benefit them.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Malay/Muslim Organisations can also play a part in helping to complement and support these initiatives.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: For example, MENDAKI had loaned out laptops to students who were awaiting approval for new ones under the NEU-PC Plus Programme when students had to suddenly pivot to home-based learning (HBL).

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The Lembaga Biasiswa Kenangan Maulud (LBKM), which has many institutional MMO members, could also galvanise community efforts in relation to education upliftment.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, the Malay Heritage Foundation has championed cultural heritage and preservation and engaged in active dialogue to recognise some of Singapore's cultural stalwarts, like the late Mr Sarkasi Said.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: How can the Malay/Muslim organisations synergise, support and complement other national initiatives?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The religious knowledge asatizahs have is important in providing expertise and guidance in non-religious sectors as well, benefiting not just the Muslim community but the wider community, too.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to know the progress into the common salary guidelines in religious institutions.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I hope, with the important, sincere work that they do, they are renumerated appropriately to attract as well as to retain talent.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: How are the salaries benchmarked against relevant sectors and what is the pay progression like as they upskill and upgrade?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, how are we galvanising the community to support this pay progression as well?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, the COVID-19 pandemic saw the need for our religious teachers to quickly pivot and adapt to ensure that religious classes and programmes could still be carried out to benefit the Muslim community.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It also raises the issue that, in addition to the continual need to upgrade religious knowledge, non-typical skills upgrading is also needed to keep up with changes that happen in society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   In a discourse written by Mufti Dr Naziruddin Nasir, which was published by Berita Harian last year, he wrote about the early days of the COVID-19 crisis, when we grappled with confusion and uncertainty on how to balance religious obligations and public safety.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, our religious and community leaders did not let the confusion hamper us and proceeded to guide the Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: As a minority Muslim community, we often face unique and multiple challenges to thrive in a non-Muslim majority society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We must ensure that ICCOS can benefit the Singapore Muslim community and help other efforts in the religious sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Can MUIS give details of the key objectives and expected outcomes from ICCOS?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, I am very heartened that many in our community have progressed and excelled in education over the past years, whether via the secular or madrasah route.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: On this point, has there been a study on this success journey and how can we continue this success rate?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Not forgetting the success rate, how can we put plans to improve those who may have missed out?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Does the Government also monitor how many from this cohort of ITE and diploma holders have progressed and attained a degree or higher?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: What are the sectors that have the least participation from our community and how do we, as a community, raise interest in those sectors so that we can seize the available opportunities?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Another group that is of concern to me is the madrasah cohort.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: How do we track the number of students that have graduated from religious universities across different parts of the Middle East?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: How has this group of graduates integrated with our multi-racial society?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister also share how does the salary package for our religious teachers or scholars compare with those teaching in secular schools?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: How are they benchmarked and how often are they being reviewed for their compensation?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I always believe that our asatizahs have to be paid competitively, or even higher, in view of the knowledge they impart and the guidance they provide to our community for this world and the hereafter.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I call on all my fellow Muslims to come forward and contribute, if a fund is needed to further develop and enhance the performance of our asatizahs and religious scholars.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that our religious teachers always have a strong aspiration to be intellectuals and scholars who that are able to innovate and shape policies in our multiracial and multi-cultural society based on Islamic principles that respect each different faith, value and culture.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Wan Rizal, take your two cuts, please.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Our religious teachers play an important role in guiding and shaping our community with the skillsets, character and citizenship so that we become a Community of Success.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This exists because we have an efficient madrasah education system.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am grateful and proud that we can see progress in our students.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the last five years, the percentage of madrasah students pursuing secondary school education has increased.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Congratulations to the Principal and teachers as well as the students on your success!

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: With the good performance of madrasah students in last year's examination, as well as in previous years, can the Minister share his plans to continue nurturing young talents in the religious sector to ensure that there is a pipeline of the next generation of religious leaders?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Muslim minority communities around the world are faced with various unique challenges that are different from the challenges faced by those living in the Muslim majority societies.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Actions and solutions to issues relevant to our society should be carefully resolved with an understanding of the context, especially in formulating knowledge, so as to help the minority Muslim community address new and complex challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the main objectives and findings that we wish to achieve through the International Conference on Communities of Success (ICCOS) and how can ICCOS benefit the Muslim community of Singapore and complement other efforts in the religious sector?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, during his annual Hari Raya get-together last year, Minister Masagos Zulkifli stressed the importance of our asatizahs being well-equipped to provide sound and relevant religious guidance for the community, especially in these times of uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Has MUIS received any feedback on these programmes?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: As we chart our way forward, our asatizahs will require additional support.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Could the Minister, thus, also share his plans to improve the leadership potential and capabilities of asatizahs for pinnacle appointments?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   As we navigate through this pandemic, our youths will require more support with strengthening their competencies for the future economy.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: The uncertainties brought forth by the pandemic would mean that we need to support our youths within and beyond the classroom.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: I am heartened to note that some programmes are already in place to assist your youths and the community, such as MENDAKI's Empowerment Programmes.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: These programmes provide our youths with opportunities to acquire life skills, build confidence and connect students to opportunities to grow their potential.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Both programmes entail competency workshops, team-bonding activities, sharing sessions and matching students to befrienders who will guide them in goal setting and motivate them to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Moreover, how effective has the existing programme been in empowering our youths to achieve their education and career aspirations?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Moving forward, our youths will need additional support due to the dynamic and ever-evolving job market.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Hence, it will have a greater role in tailoring existing mentorship approaches to meet our youths' needs.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Could the Minister elaborate on its future plans for the ITE Empowerment Programmes and whether it will be adjusted to meet the dynamic needs of our youths?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: (In Malay):   In the recent Budget debate, I supported the plan to expand the KidSTART and UPLIFT programmes to more children across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: It underlines the Government's strong commitment to address inequality as early as possible.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: In Singapore, no one will be left behind especially our children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Early childhood education and good support will give them a strong foundation and a good start in their educational journey.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Since its inception, M3 agencies have been very supportive of all efforts to strengthen the family and education institutions.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: As such, I would like to ask the Minister how M3 agencies and their volunteers can work more closely with the Government to ensure that children in rental housing get early help, so that they are not left behind when they enter primary school.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Chairman, permission to take both my cuts together, please.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, volunteers at M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol have made considerable efforts in bringing digital skills to our community through events held at Pasir Ris East CC.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: At our M3 Goes Digital event, students learnt to assemble a jet engine using augmented reality (AR) and how to use 3D printers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Parents also found out more about safe digital practices while seniors learnt to use digital tools from our volunteers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: We must provide opportunities for our youths to acquire the skills required in growth industries, so that they can aspire and gain the confidence to pursue careers in new industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: What can MENDAKI do to provide platforms for our youths who wish to pursue a career in these growth industries?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Youths also benefit from a mentor as someone who they can turn to for advice.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Having a support system can inspire and motivate youths.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can MENDAKI provide an update on the progress of our youth mentoring programmes?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can we work with Malay/Muslim professionals and industry partners who can help our youths better plan for their future careers?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, we have seen immense changes to the economy these past two years.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Digitalisation is at the core of many businesses.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Concern for environmental sustainability has become a key consideration for many industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Employment opportunities continuously evolve and work from home or other flexible work arrangements are becoming the norm in some industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How do we increase the employability of our workforce and provide platforms for our community to explore new opportunities?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can MENDAKI streamline its efforts with national agencies and corporate partners to ensure that our Malay/Muslim community is future-ready and poised to benefit from new employment opportunities?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We also have a shortage of Malay workers in certain sectors such as tech financing, green financing, banking, as well as in the developing sectors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, our goal must not only be to get more people within our community into permanent jobs and to ensure that they can be upskilled to get better jobs with higher wages and job security, but to work in the developing sectors in future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Various initiatives are already underway to build a competent and future-ready workforce among the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another example is M3, which leads many initiatives, including organising career fairs and providing training and career advice.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What is the Government's thinking on streamlining our efforts to build a competent, future-ready workforce in the Malay/Muslim community?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there specific detailed efforts to reallocate and concentrate more Malay/Muslim talent, both young and mature, in emerging growth sectors, such as through permanent internship opportunities and sectoral level scholarships with various corporations?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must have sectoral focus and have a deeper collaboration with the private sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In English): We will also need to focus on cultivating a culture of learning and upskilling within the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have a few suggestions on that front.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, we can tie up career sharing programmes with other initiatives.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I recently had the opportunity to visit a clinic where Lawyers@M³ executed Lasting Power of Attorney for my residents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We could perhaps wrap in a sharing on mid-career switch to lawyering, which can reach the applicants, as well as their children who accompanied them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, we can encourage our Malay/Muslim workers, especially the younger ones, to be adaptable and to try new things.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our workers should be encouraged to venture abroad, through overseas secondments and training opportunities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third, we can facilitate interaction and cross-pollination of ideas between the Malay/Muslim workforce and the rest of the workforce, among Chinese, Indian and Malay Chambers and with corporates.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are areas where the community has subject matter expertise, for example, Islamic finance, which some of my Chinese and European colleagues are also interested to learn more.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: By teaching, one can reinforce his or her understanding and expertise in a particular area as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: No matter the specific initiatives we implement, we ought to have a coordinated approach to help our Malay/Muslim workers develop into a competent, future-ready workforce.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, I would like to thank the Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   When Singapore became independent in 1965, many had thought that we would not survive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To ensure our survival, the Government's priority was to ensure access to affordable education, housing and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This became the bedrock for us to build strong families and caring communities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even after more than five decades, our Singapore story continues to centre around a shared vision of a society that provides opportunities for all, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We were united and worked as one to uplift the lives of Singaporeans, including our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More Malay workers were also employed in fast-growing sectors such as information and communications, as well as financial and insurance services.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened by this as it reflects the good progress of our education and employment outcomes over the decades.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the past few years, I have spoken about the three "C"s that make us a Community of Success – character, competence and citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, I will focus on the development of our competencies, even as we build on our achievements to propel the community towards further success.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will be done through three key strategies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While our economic progress has benefited many Singaporeans, it has also given rise to new challenges, particularly towards the vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Rising social inequality has become a common concern for many advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Such situations make it easy for new fault lines to emerge between different segments of society and threaten our social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In Singapore, we can avoid such a situation if we continue to ensure that social mobility remains alive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Therefore, for the vulnerable segments of our community, the Government and the community must continue to work hand-in-hand to ensure that they are well supported through the different life milestones.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, the Government has rolled out several initiatives, such as support measures for early childhood education, to better prepare our young for the future – this is the best way to ensure social mobility.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For our community, these have been further amplified with community initiatives by the M3 agencies – namely, MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA – as well as those undertaken by other Malay/Muslim organisations, to further amplify support for those in need.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister Mohamad Maliki will share our plans on how M3 reinforces our network of care for our community and families, as we empower and engage this segment of our community to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, Yayasan MENDAKI is celebrating its 40th anniversary.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some of us would have remembered then-Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew's speech at the opening of the MENDAKI Congress at the Singapore Conference Hall in 1982, where he called for MENDAKI to raise the educational levels and thus the living standards of the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am pleased that MENDAKI had applied his advice over the past 40 years.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In working closely with its partners, MENDAKI had contributed to the very encouraging progress shown by the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Better education outcomes have also led to better career opportunities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we cannot be satisfied now and end our journey here, especially when we are faced with stiffer global competition and even more rapid changes in technology.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad will elaborate on MENDAKI's efforts to expand support beyond the classroom to offer more strategic programmes, in fulfilling the evolving needs of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These efforts stress the need to imbue a culture of lifelong learning in our community, especially through upskilling, so that we remain relevant in the new economy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will elaborate on MUIS' plans to shape a credible and resilient religious sector in the final speech of this segment.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the last few decades, we have seen generations of Malay families do well and move up in life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we still have some who still face challenges and need help as they progress.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Member of Parliament Faisal Manap raised this issue during the Budget debate recently, saying that the community has regressed and families in rental flats are living in cramped conditions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is sad to hear how Mr Faisal Manap had portrayed the plight of these families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the increase in number of households in rental flats is in tandem with the higher supply of 1- and 3-room public rental flats in the past decade provided by HDB.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, the public rental households include young families who need temporary accommodation while they stabilise their income and savings.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Another group are flat owners who were not able to purchase another flat after selling their previous flats for various reasons, including divorce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prior to moving into their rental flats, many would be living with extended family members in a crowded environment, far less conducive than what they have now.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For these families, public rental flats provide improved living conditions, as the much-needed shelter for them, as they work through their various socio-economic challenges and aspire to be home owners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a community, we are determined to uplift the vulnerable families, especially those with young children, to secure a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We set up Project DIAN@M3 last year to support families in our public rental flats to achieve greater social mobility.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will reinforce our network of care for the community through M3 in three ways.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We intend and we will invest early in our children's education, so that we can create a strong foundation for life for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will empower families to achieve their aspirations to be home owners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will enhance community capabilities to strengthen support for families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, allow me to share some of the challenges that families staying in public rental flats face.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Recently, I met Ahmad, not his real name, and his wife.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They live in a 2-room public rental flat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both are 26 years old and have three young children between two and six years old.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The young family is faced with financial difficulty and other challenges.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both grew up without stable home environments nor guidance from other family members.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ahmad's parents and his elder siblings are divorced.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As for Ahmad's wife, her mother passed away when she was two years old, while her father was mostly absent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have to raise three children at such a young age, without guidance from their elders.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The story of Ahmad's family reflects the situation faced by young families in rental flats.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They are who we call, first-timer households – families who have neither purchased nor owned a flat but certainly have the potential to do so and do well in life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They feel overwhelmed by their circumstances as they lack the necessary skills and social support networks.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We can strengthen the support network for these families and guide them to the resources and support available.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will take an upstream approach to support them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will help them stabilise and increase their incomes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: About one-third are single-parent families while the rest are married couples.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will help them overcome whatever barriers they face, including supporting them to upgrade their skills through training and upskilling, as well as childcare issues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In total, there are about 3,800 Malay children aged six and below living in public rental flats whose parents are first timers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: About 60% of them have at least one child aged three and younger.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The early years in a child's life are crucial in laying a strong foundation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This goes beyond preparing our young children academically, but also for them to develop well physically, mentally and socially.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the Malay saying goes, "bend the bamboo while it is still a shoot" – which means to mould a person while one is still young.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the past, most children attended school only at Primary 1 as preschool was not viewed seriously.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, it was called "sekolah makan" and many did not attend preschool.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, around nine in 10 children in Singapore attend preschool by the age of four.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: International research tells us that attending quality preschool early, from around age three, can boost children's confidence and social skills and help prepare them for school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, we will endeavour to convince and urge these parents to send their children to preschool early, so that their children have at least three years of education before they enter Primary 1.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I share Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's view that more families can benefit from KidSTART.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: KidSTART is a programme that empowers parents and caregivers to provide infant care and childcare.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through home visits by KIDSTART facilitators, they will also be given appropriate learning tools as well as opportunities to practise effective parent-child interaction techniques.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: KIDSTART facilitators will also guide them on the appropriate nutritional needs of their children and ways to stimulate their children's brain development to harness their growth potential.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These parents will also be assisted in enrolling their children in preschool.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Regular screening of the child's development and maternal well-being are also conducted from the antenatal stage to when the child is three years old, so that timely interventions can be introduced should issues arise.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about M3's efforts to ensure that young children in public rental flats receive early intervention.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through Project DIAN@M3, our M3 volunteers will work closely with KidSTART to strengthen support for Malay families living in public rental flats with young children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will start with the three blocks under the Project DIAN@M3 pilot.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our volunteers will work closely with KidSTART officers, visit them regularly, support their child's development and befriend these families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As I mentioned earlier, there are about 3,800 children today aged six and below from Malay families living in public rental flats.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I know that many are concerned about the future of these children, and I urge them to step forward to volunteer with us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Your acts of service and compassion have the ability to change the future of these children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For children entering the formal school environment, we also want to improve their performance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will provide tools and resources through M3 programmes, such as the KelasMateMatika@CC (KMM) and KelasSiapSekolah (KSS), so that they can succeed in school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about the success of KMM and KSS.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2021, 83% of KMM participants came from low-income families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Parents have also benefited from KSS, with 90% of them reporting that they will use the approaches shared to guide their children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MENDAKI is also going upstream to strengthen support to children in Mathematics in the early primary school years, instead of at Primary 6 currently.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For Primary 1 to Primary 3 children who have been identified as needing additional support, MENDAKI will bring coaches to their homes to provide one-on-one Mathematics lessons.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will mean a more intensive approach which will require more resources.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are prepared to allocate the necessary resources.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The coaches will guide these children at their own pace of learning, recognising that each person has their own strengths.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are confident that the coaches' presence in the homes will inspire and empower the parents to be more involved in their children's education.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These upstream steps may be small but are crucial towards developing our children's competencies in their early years and building their confidence and resilience.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the long run, efforts in early childhood education will help achieve greater inter-generational mobility for these families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, Project DIAN@M3 also aims to help households in rental flats improve their incomes and work towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We strengthen wrap-around support for families in rental flats by linking up these families with community and national programmes, including MSF's Community Link, MOE's UPLIFT and ECDA's KidSTART, to complement the Government's effort with an approach that aligns with the Malay community's culture and values.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To facilitate this, we have formed the Project DIAN Steering Committee, comprising senior officers from the relevant Government and community agencies, to coordinate efforts among Government agencies and community partners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For more efficient service delivery, we have formed an Operations Group at the local level in each of the three pilot blocks.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This local Operations Group comprises officers from the same Government agencies and community partners as the Project DIAN Steering Committee.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through this group, we will further understand each family's circumstances and needs, and work together to provide comprehensive support for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We acknowledge the important role of volunteers in the journey with these families and in guiding them every step of the way – from supporting their children's early education, to equipping parents with skillsets to secure good jobs and stable incomes to buy their own flat.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past few years, volunteers from MESRA and the Malay Activity Executive Committees (MAECs) have expanded their roles beyond just organising cultural events.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, they work together with volunteers from the mosques and professional groups to engage and conduct needs assessment of Malay households in public rental units using similar forms as the MSF's ComLink programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will streamline efforts and thus allows us to provide customised services that meet the unique needs of each family.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Nadia Admad Samdin also asked about the success indicators and long-term outcomes of Project DIAN@M3.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our aim is to strengthen the children's early childhood education to help them secure a brighter future, and for families to achieve stability, so that they can be self-reliant and eventually have social mobility.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will track each family's progress in meeting their goal to own their homes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are confident that these efforts will pay off.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we all know that this process will take time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked for an update on the Family and Inmates Throughcare Assistance Haven, or FITRAH programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Seventy-five percent of these supported offenders are male.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, I am happy to see many Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) coming forward to support us in this effort, such as through FITRAH's MMO Alliance Network.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I look forward to more MMOs partnering M3 to uplift our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, without the support of the community, the reach and impact of our programmes in uplifting the vulnerable will be limited.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our volunteers play an important role in reaching out to families to understand their concerns, conducting needs assessment and befriending them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of our volunteers have displayed empathy, patience and resilience.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have been tirelessly helping these families work and walk the journey to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To expand our network of care, especially to the families with children aged six and below living in public rental flats, we need more volunteers to come forward to support us in this effort.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need volunteers who can inspire hope in families, engage them regularly over an extended period of time, thereby building rapport and trust with them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I encourage more from the community to step forward and contribute in whatever way they can.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite restrictions during COVID-19, our M3@Towns have done well serving the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our M3@Towns also supported residents through ground-up initiatives, such as the "Jom Surf!" – "Jom", Melayu word for "Come" – which equips our seniors with digital literacy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With guidance from our young volunteers, seniors built their confidence in using technology by learning how to use WhatsApp, Singpass and TraceTogether app.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I attended one of these sessions recently and was heartened to see the enthusiasm of both our young volunteers and our senior learners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, we will continue our efforts to strengthen our programmes and outreach to targeted segments – our children, our families and the community – to build up their competencies and empower them to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This spirit of caring for one another binds us together and we will leave no one behind as we build our Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's progress is built upon a shared purpose and a sense of togetherness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Malay/Muslim community aspires to be a Community of Success – to contribute to the growth of our nation and create opportunities to uplift our families and those around us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Skilling, reskilling and upskilling are vital to succeed in the future, especially in this economy, as we look beyond COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government, in partnership with industry and the community, is ramping up its efforts to better position our Malay community for employment in growth sectors while inculcating lifelong learning into our DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will focus on upstream support by strengthening mentoring and early career guidance for youths in schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, we have several new initiatives for our students in the ITEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also enhance scholarship opportunities and financial support to help students pursue their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For those who have entered the workforce, we will partner industries to provide upskilling and direct emplacement opportunities for workers, especially in growth sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, each child deserves an opportunity in life to actualise their potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, there may be times when they face challenges which weigh heavy on them, causing some to lose motivation and hope.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Thus, having a support system is critical to motivate them to stay resilient and keep on the right path to fulfil their aspirations as well as their potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is why MENDAKI is investing and strengthening its mentoring programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We believe that our youths can benefit from a mentor outside the classroom – a role model whom they can turn to for advice, look up to and learn from to realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, we want to provide opportunities for those who have succeeded to give back to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Sharael Taha asked for an update on MENDAKI's mentoring programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also glad to share that 10 community partners from the Community Leaders Forum (CLF), including the Majulah Community, Malay Youth Literary Association (4PM), AMP Singapore and Singapore Tenkasi, have come on board to conduct mentoring programmes for their own beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the YMO, we are now making mentoring more accessible for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I call on more from the community to step forward as mentors to help our youths thrive as successful adults.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To address Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin's query, mentoring programmes from MENDAKI and M3 Focus Area 3 partners are open to all Malay/Muslim students, including madrasah students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, these programmes aim to expand the social circle and promote bonding among students from the various backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have been taking this inclusive approach for other MENDAKI programmes, too, such as the Future Ready initiatives and career programmes, which are designed to prepare our youths for meaningful careers, no matter their background.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Abdul Samad asked about the students in our Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On average, about 30 Malay graduates from each ITE cohort progressed to the Autonomous Universities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: You can imagine the pathways and I think it is quite commendable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their employment outcomes are broadly comparable to their peers from other ethnic groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, this year, we will provide more support for our youths in ITE to complement the Government's efforts to enhance applied education in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Piloted in 2019, MENDAKI’s Empowerment Programme at ITE seeks to build support systems and help students acquire life skills, develop confidence and grow their potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman's question, the Empowerment Programme has benefited more than 2,000 mentees since its inception.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the programme, MENDAKI has managed to enrol one in every five Malay/Muslim NITEC students in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One student who benefited from the ITE Empowerment Programme is Muhammad Roth Isaac from ITE College West.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Isaac took on a part-time job to help his family of four after his father's income was affected by the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Even though Isaac is just a teenager, he had to deal with the pressure and responsibility of juggling school and supporting his family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Fortunately, he had a caring mentor, Mr Sandeep Krishna, who constantly checked on his well-being and helped him with his studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sandeep currently works as a Network Engineer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Despite his heavy work commitment, he sets aside time for mentoring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sandeep recalls the challenges he faced as a student not too long ago and, hence, he believes in the value of guiding youths towards their potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sandeep befriended Isaac and motivated him to remain in school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Isaac remained focused and managed to achieve a 3.7 GPA in his first year of NITEC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, well done, Isaac, and thank you, Mr Sandeep!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We need to help more students like Isaac to do well – not only for themselves, but for their families and the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means tailoring the mentoring approach for each mentee to achieve specific objectives, depending on their circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The #amPowered programme will also be progressively made available under the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme (MTS) and at our M3 Towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We agree with Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman and Mr Sharael Taha that our students can benefit from structured career guidance, especially to growth sectors, such as information and communications, financial and insurance services, and professional services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Thus, to complement the mentoring programmes, MENDAKI will deploy Care Advisors at each of the YouthSpaces in the three ITE Colleges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their role is to guide students on possible education pathways and connect them to skilling or emplacement opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Care Advisors can also be found at MENDAKI's satellite centres to serve the Malay/Muslim community at large.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, over the years, MENDAKI has provided bursaries, study loans and subsidies, so that financial circumstances do not impede our students from achieving success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Moving forward, MENDAKI will focus on providing targeted financial support for the developmental needs of our students and broaden the opportunities for them to build career aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The scholarship is in partnership with three local Universities – NUS, NTU and SMU – and will cover the undergraduate tuition fees for most degree programmes in these Universities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: GIC will provide structured internships, job rotations, networking and mentorship for the scholarship recipients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, they can expect an exciting and purposeful career with GIC upon their graduation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The GIC-MENDAKI Scholarship is the latest effort by MENDAKI to collaborate with the industry to provide a springboard for our youths into careers in fast-growing industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This follows other scholarships, such as the MENDAKI-MiRXES scholarship formed last year in Life and Biomedical Sciences, and the SIA-MENDAKI scholarship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These scholarships provide students with priority internship opportunities and secure employment upon their graduation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will continue to expand these opportunities and I urge all Malay/Muslim students to work hard and seize them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The generosity of our corporate partners and community has enabled us to provide more support to deserving students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, over $1 million of ETF bursaries was established, including the ETF-Gafoor PropNex Bursary and Math Coaching Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On top of school necessities, this bursary would directly pay for students' development programmes in Mathematics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope this targeted approach will be the way forward for MENDAKI to better support the immediate needs of our students and their growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I have explained how we intend to prepare our youths for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, let me now elaborate on our plans to provide more directed and targeted support to emplace our Malay/Muslim workers into growth industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, I have explained how we intend to strengthen upstream mentoring and career guidance efforts to help our youths achieve their dreams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will also enhance financial support and scholarship opportunities to help students pursue their aspirations to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For those in the workforce, we will build up their competencies, so that they stay relevant for new and growing industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, MENDAKI conducted 15 career fairs, participated by over 700 job seekers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Out of these, more than 300 workers were placed in jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As part of MENDAKI's transformation efforts, we will expand our partnerships with national training agencies to emplace our Malay/Muslim workers in growth industries, such as in technology and the green economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Mr Sharael Taha also asked how these efforts will benefit our new job seekers and mid-career workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also gave a few suggestions which we will study further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Do allow me to explain the Government's approach in more detail.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will build on our partnership with SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) to promote capability development programmes to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will augment national efforts by mobilising MENDAKI's Care Advisors at our five satellite centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
