speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These 111 represent over two-thirds of the total number of arts and heritage charities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many charities have also embarked on their own fundraising for the first time to diversify their revenue streams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The top-up will encourage cultural philanthropy and enhance the sustainability of the arts and heritage sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CMF will complement existing initiatives to provide stronger support to smaller charities to develop their own governance and fundraising capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our cultural heritage plays an important role in growing a strong, confident society by anchoring our own unique Singaporean identity and telling stories that are our own and that define and inspire us as a country.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Padang, for example, has borne witness to many significant national events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The site is an instantly recognisable enduring testament to our history as a people and as a country.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We were very proud some time ago when our hawker culture was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) list.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are now looking at a second UNESCO ICH nomination.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have sought views on them and we will think about them a bit more, think about how else and what are the possible nominations and will continue to engage with our relevant stakeholders, as well as the public, before reaching a decision.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked for an update on our long-term vision for the arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Even as we work on the here and now, and Members will see that we have many initiatives on the here and now, we have kept a clear eye on the future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since mid-2021, we have been actively engaging stakeholders in the sector to develop a vision for the next Arts and Heritage Plans and will further engage stakeholders this year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Arts and Heritage Plans 2.0 will continue to build upon the vital role played by the arts and heritage in deepening our national identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Again, Minister of State Low Yen Ling will give more details on the Arts and Heritage Plans 2.0.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Darryl David and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about strategies to bring sports participation back, and Mr Mark Chay asked a series of questions about sports entertainment and, in particular, digital content, to promote Singapore's culture and identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Miss Cheng, in particular, spoke with such passion about the National Stadium.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think she showed her vintage naming those players, but I would suggest that we look forward as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Irfan Fandi, Gabriel Quak, Jacob Mahler are some names of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have been supporting the sports and fitness industry to enhance their value proposition through digitalisation, to transform the way they present and, in turn, the way we consume and experience activities and sporting content.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is very encouraging and we will continue with this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To date, more than 600 businesses were supported by the SRP.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The SRP will sustain the momentum of innovation, such as through the Enterprise Innovation and Capabilities Development Grant (InnoGrant), which supports businesses in applying technology and innovative solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through these, some sports businesses are fundamentally transforming the way we experience sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, SportSG's "Blended" initiative supports businesses through areas, such as data analytics and fan engagement, so that they can better develop hybrid experiences which better connect with the audience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With Blended's support, 18 hybrid events reached over 90,000 participants.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One such event is RIDEnjoySG, an innovative campaign that encourages participants to cycle safely on bike paths and park connectors whilst, at the same time, enjoying real-world rewards via location-based challenges and augmented reality.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We progressively resumed sporting activities and also hosted several international events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2022, we want to step it up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is designed to reinvigorate Singapore sports, bring people back to play and enjoy sports together and, through sports, reconnect with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Bring Sport Back will focus on three key elements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we will safely reintroduce mass participation events for all, through more community events and sports festivals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To facilitate this, SportSG will be opening a grant call to fund mass participation events at up to $50,000 per award under the Blended Events Grant – Bring Sport Back edition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we will ramp up community participation in sports through enhanced programming and more group activities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Currently, more than 170 facilities have already resumed "5 against 5" team sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are working on resuming larger team sports capacities across more facilities around Singapore, bringing it back to full capacity in several phases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will roll out more leagues and competitions for people of all ages under the ActiveSG umbrella.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include the ActiveSG Cup launch and ActiveSG Leagues for Athletics, Badminton and Canoeing.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: ActiveSG Academies and Clubs will ramp up the capacity of high-quality programmes, to strengthen sport development, social integration, health and wellness and inculcate strong values of resilience and determination, values that one can get through sport participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will also offer additional pathways for youth development at the elite level.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also picked up growing interest in pickleball – I think some Members may be familiar with that sport – an increasingly popular sport, particularly among our seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to keep our ears to the ground and will, in this case, for pickleball, increase the frequency of this and any other popular activities that will bring people back to sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we will optimise facilities and spaces to encourage people to return and to play together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These spaces will be community-driven, serving the unique needs of our different neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include repurposing spaces for a range of sports and converting underused spaces into outdoor gyms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We hope that these measures will encourage Singaporeans to resume sporting and wellness activities safely.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One of the values that Singaporeans hold dear is inclusivity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must build a society where everyone, regardless of their own circumstances in life, can take part and can flourish.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I appreciate very much Miss Cheng Li Hui's and Mr Darryl David's questions on inclusive sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are several aspects to this, for which we have a few broad initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I spoke during my earlier Parliamentary Motion last year about the unique ability of sports to enhance an individual's own self-confidence and to transform community attitudes towards a person with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sports are one arena where we can, and, indeed, we should, level everyone up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through sports, we can empower persons with disabilities in deeply profound ways to help them realise their full potential and raise their visibility and prominence in society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For many para-athletes, their stories attest to the value of sports in Singapore, playing a pivotal part in building an inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Para Sport Academy will bring us one step closer, one step further along this journey, ensuring our para-athletes will have an equal platform and as much opportunity as any other to scale the pinnacle of sporting excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Both of these initiatives will provide enhanced opportunities for those with disabilities or from less privileged backgrounds to achieve their hopes and dreams and use sports to uplift themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, will share more details on these two initiatives, as well as other sports developments to look forward to.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Ms Joan Pereira said, this year marks the 20th anniversary of our Inter-racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many Members, in fact, know that our IRCCs have been instrumental in shaping our interfaith harmony over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their mission to strengthen our social cohesion remains as important today as it was 20 years ago, when we first set it up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: IRCC was first formed in 2002, at a time when the world was reeling in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks and Singapore had also just uncovered the Jemaah Islamiyah plot to attack embassies on our own soil.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We now have IRCCs in every constituency, with over 1,500 members comprising key leaders from various religious organisations, grassroots, community leaders and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The IRCCs have, over the years, been a critical bridge between the different community groups, building bridges, building trust and friendships and just doing day-to-day things, so that the lived experience enhances those bonds.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On average, the IRCCs organise over 250 activities each year, including dialogues on different faiths, practices and festivals, and joint collaborations to support one another in times of need.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We agree with Ms Joan Pereira that we should do more to open the common spaces, to listen and learn about other faiths, religions and practices, without prejudice.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The IRCCs also act as a conduit between the Government and community by highlighting issues emerging on the ground, providing insights and ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Fahmi Bin Aliman asked how we plan to step up social cohesion efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked how we plan to keep IRCCs effective and relevant and promote a more inclusive nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are bridges and connectors on the ground across communities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we are also operating and very quickly moving into a rapidly-changing landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will, therefore, have to refresh our IRCCs, so that they stand ready to respond to future challenges, such as evolving societal attitudes, increasing fault lines and the pervasive impact of social media on race and religious relations, like some Members have highlighted earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must also anticipate the challenges in the next bound.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Workgroup comprises members who are experienced IRCC leaders, representatives from religious organisations, civil society leaders and groups and community partners as well as youth leaders who play an integral and instrumental part in shaping what we want to be doing in the future to promote racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the next few months, the Workgroup will consult widely with a range of community stakeholders, identify the strengths and challenges faced by the IRCCs, look at some of the issues, look at how we can tackle them and put forward their recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I look forward to the Workgroup presenting its recommendations later on this year and I will share them with Members of this House.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, Madam, Ms Joan Pereira asked how we can continue to strengthen community life at the neighbourhood level and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked how we can increase care and cohesiveness in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the heart of our communities and neighbourhoods are the Residents Committees (RC) and Residents' Networks (RN) centres.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The way to increase care, cohesiveness, bonds on the ground, is not necessarily to come up with special projects or special events to bring people together, but to share as part of our daily lived experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When you step out of your home, when you go down to the common areas in the community, how can we foster that bond?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman and Miss Cheng Li Hui also asked how MCCY plans to make volunteerism and care a greater part of our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To do so, the SG Cares movement and People's Association (PA) will generate multiple pathways for volunteerism so that everyone can play a part for the common good.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are several initiatives and I will just highlight one that the PA is studying and will implement shortly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is, to broaden opportunities for volunteerism on the ground where, as far as possible, we can do it on a fluid, informal and flexible basis.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, working with the community to support volunteers, formal and informal, who wish to work on specific causes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will support volunteers in causes that they care about.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we want to partner already existing networks on the ground to encourage community involvement and to reach out to potential networks of volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we will support these community volunteers in their projects through grants, cross-sharing of volunteering opportunities and also providing resources, together with other agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The PA's efforts also complement ongoing SG Cares' efforts to expand the base of volunteers through working with community partners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Gerald Giam, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Gan Thiam Poh all asked about our processes to deal with such disputes and how we can enhance the use of mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members will be aware that in 2014, the Community Dispute Management Framework (CDMF) was introduced.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The framework was aimed at facilitating effective resolution of common neighbourly disputes to seek to foster a more harmonious living environment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MinLaw, MCCY, MND and MHA are involved in this review.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I also mentioned in my MinLaw COS speech, our agencies are exploring a range of enhancements to the framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These cover both upstream measures to promote prosocial norms and downstream measures to enhance our response to disputes, addressing situations where disputes would benefit from mediation and possibly dispute resolution at the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Oftentimes, they are also best suited for mediation, which provides not just a quick, friendly, informal process to deal with, but also one which, as far as possible, preserves the existing relationship between the two neighbours – one that is amicable and conciliatory in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, at present, as some Members have pointed out, the mediation take-up rate remains low despite this being a proven effective means to resolve disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are, therefore, considering three broad areas of enhancements to better manage such disagreements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we will collaborate with residents to strengthen the spirit of neighbourliness and graciousness through shared norms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In her MND COS speech, my colleague, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, spoke about forming a Community Advisory Panel (CAP) on Neighbourhood Noise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This panel will seek to build consensus through community norms that can be a useful guide for determining acceptable behaviours among neighbours and also serve as a useful reference point for agencies in advising residents to be considerate neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we are considering ways to improve our dispute resolution mechanisms, both in mediation and in the CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For mediation, we intend to increase the take-up rate for mediation, both formal and informal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Community Mediation Centre (CMC) has a high settlement rate – I mentioned this previously and I will mention it again.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This shows that when parties avail themselves of this process, formal mediation is very effective and should be the preferred mechanism for resolving neighbourly tensions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are looking into increasing awareness on the benefits of mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CMC has been using social media to promote its services and has also been reaching out to frontline officers to promote the benefits of mediation and the referral process.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are exploring more varied modes of mediation to increase accessibility, for example, doing online virtual mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is so that neighbours may resolve differences amicably as far as possible, without first going through the CDRT process, which is adjudicatory and often zero-sum in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are also considering possible consequences for parties who fail to attend mediation and, yet, want to pursue a claim at CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Gerald Giam suggested that we allow adverse inferences to be drawn and we will consider that.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will then make it easier for the CMC to have its settlement agreements enforced as an order of Court.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will work on programmes to better equip our community leaders with the skills to informally mediate between residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Very often, they are also a neighbour themselves and can be the best first responder to the situation to understand the context, the lay of the land and, quite possibly, be the respected person that both neighbours can look up to.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are the ingredients for a successful mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about the CDRT's caseload.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In cases where respondents breach the orders granted by CDRT, claimants have gone on to apply for Special Directions, Compliance Bonds and Exclusion Orders from CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Gerald Giam raised a point about uploading of evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The current requirement for audio and video recordings, which often are the most direct way in which you can show and substantiate your position to the CDRT, these are usually submitted using CD or DVD due to the need to preserve data integrity and security.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Nonetheless, the Courts are continually reviewing their processes and will take into account Mr Giam's point and assess the viability of alternatives to submit evidence in Court.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the meantime, Court users who require assistance to submit audio or video recordings to the CDRT can approach the CDRT Registry for assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third and, finally, we are looking to enhance processes and resources for a targeted response that can better assess the nature and scope of a complaint and attend to them quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One possibility could be a team of ground responders empowered to collect and share evidence or reports with the CDRT to alleviate the evidential burden for parties involved.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More details will be announced as we continue with this review and the findings are firmed up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Darryl David asked for an update on TeamSG's preparations for the major games in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, all of us cheered our Olympians and Paralympians as they flew the Singapore flag high and proud in Tokyo.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We celebrated the achievements of Loh Kean Yew and Aloysius Yapp who reached the pinnacles of their respective sports last year, in badminton and in cue sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Shayna Ng and Yip Pin Xiu, names which I am sure all of you recognise, continued to inspire us through world-class performances in bowling and swimming.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Colin Soon won four Gold medals at the Asian Youth Para Games for swimming; Maximilian Maeder won the Under-19 World Championships for kite foiling; and Izaac Quek, who is competing at the World Table Tennis (WTT) Singapore Smash, won the Under-15 Singles title for table tennis.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will have a busy sporting calendar in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will have the Hanoi SEA Games in May, the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in July and August, the Hangzhou Asian Games and the Hangzhou Para Games in September and October, respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am confident that our TeamSG athletes will continue to fly our flag high and inspire us with their resilience, fortitude and solidarity, the very same qualities that will enable Singapore to progress and develop on multiple fronts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have spoken at length in Parliament earlier this year and last year on the Government's support for high performance sports and our TeamSG athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to do so and enable each of our athletes to put their best foot forward in these competitions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We encourage all to support our TeamSG athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Much of the impact that COVID-19 has on the sectors we care for is intangible and often latent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have to ensure that we do not suffer a deficit in social resilience in our society, even as we strive to protect lives and livelihoods in this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They show us who we are, how far we have come and what we cherish, value and aspire to.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Resilience in defeat and grace in victory – these are qualities that are like a microcosm of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As our athletes and artists succeed, so does our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More importantly, in sports, art, culture and heritage, we see that our diversity in race, colour and creed is, in fact, our strength.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These distinctions do not divide us; they enable us, they make us stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Whether it is on the playing field or under the stage lights, our athletes and artists show us that what matters are what we bring to the table – our unique gifts, talents and experiences – and our shared dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The qualities we see on the stage or on the pitch – grace under pressure, commitment to excellence, dedication to one another, to our team mates – are the very same ones we hold dear in society, that inspire in us pride, unity and courage, and the ability to dream even bigger together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Kudos to our arts and culture organisations and practitioners – they have responded boldly and creatively to the challenges brought on by the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through their craft and artistic contributions, they have provided soothing balm and comfort to us all in a difficult time like this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are grateful for their resilience and perseverance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Looking ahead, for the year 2022, we will continue to work closely with our arts and culture community to chart our path towards recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will enlarge our longer-term plans with the aims to foster in Singapore a resilient, sustainable and future-ready arts and culture ecosystem that: one, enriches and inspires lives; two, unites us as a nation, with pride in our shared heritage; and three, enhances Singapore's shine as a global city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we look forward to our arts and culture sector recovering even stronger than before from the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our practitioners have reached new audiences, created new experiences and enhanced existing capabilities while developing new ones in areas like digital showcases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is the result of our collective resolve over the last two years as the arts and culture community collaborate and support one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Darryl David will be pleased to know that we will do even more to sustain the momentum and enable the sector to build on these gains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will continue to defray venue hire costs for our practitioners, as we progressively resume activities and welcome back larger audiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Introduced last year as part of the ACRP, the Organisation Transformation Grant (OTG) has attracted keen interest from arts and culture organisations and practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To sustain support for transformation, NHB will incorporate the OTG into its existing grants, such as the Heritage Research Grant, as well as the Minor and Major Project Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The grants will also be open to Business Associations to encourage transformation efforts in our historic districts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Projects previously supported under the ACRP OTG that have longer-term potential for further development, can tap on the STF to push ahead and transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will empower the sector to leverage digital technologies to pursue new artistic, cultural and business opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through digitalisation, the sector can enhance their existing revenue streams, as well as improve productivity and organisational effectiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recently launched the Arts and Culture Digital Roadmap on 28 February to equip and enhance the digital journey of our arts and culture organisations and practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They can use the Digital Roadmap, which has a self-assessment checklist, to gauge their level of digital readiness and learn about the range of digital solutions and funding schemes available to businesses, charities and individuals that can support such efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Mark Chay pointed out, we can showcase our unique culture to local, as well as overseas audiences by using more digital content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, Ding Yi Music Company brought their triennial international composition festival called "Composium" online last year, which led to its musicians and the compositions of local composers, such as Cultural Medallion recipients Eric Watson and Law Wai Lun, reaching international audiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the coming months, MCCY, NAC and NHB will be engaging our arts and culture organisations and practitioners through roadshows and workshops to promote awareness of the Digital Roadmap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also provide tailored support to those who require assistance to digitalise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Details of these efforts will be made available on the websites of all three organisations, once they are ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, an independent producer, Ms Nurhafezhah Maznan, created a structured programme for eight young theatre directors to learn from 17 artists and other creatives on how to direct works in Malay and Tamil.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to deepen our support for SEPs by incorporating the SEPG into NAC's existing Presentation and Participation (P&P) and Capability Development (CD) grants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling will be glad to know that, through this move, priority will be given to grant applications initiated by or targeted at SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we are committed to creating conditions in the arts and culture sector for livelihoods to thrive, with targeted support for SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will increase opportunities for capacity development for SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, NAC will raise greater awareness of the skills and competencies that our SEPs need to help them make informed choices for their career progression.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will also work with partners to mount training courses in new and emerging areas, such as e-pedagogy and digital arts education programme development, for arts instructors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, NAC will work with industry partners to ensure better protection and working conditions for our SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will promote the adoption of best practices among organisations which engage SEPs – from the signing of formal contracts to improving contractual obligations between the parties and recognising our SEPs for their skills and contributions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, NAC will pilot new ways for SEPs to create value in the arts sector and beyond.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC has observed some enterprising SEPs, especially in the last two years, developing artist-business partnership and testing new ways to work with enterprises working on sustainability solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will support SEPs to push boundaries and contribute to the broader creative economy, as well as to collaborate with one another and new partners – such as local businesses – from other sectors in new and innovative ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage our SEPs to make full use of the available grants to sustain their practices, collaborate on new initiatives and develop new capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We look forward to our SEPs' continued contribution to Singapore's arts and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of the newest additions to this growing pool is the Singapore Art Museum (SAM) at Tanjong Pagar Distripark (TPD).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I visited SAM at TPD just two months ago with Minister Edwin Tong in January for the 10th edition of the Singapore Art Week (SAW) 2022 and we saw for ourselves how a former industrial warehouse was turned into a fascinating location for experimental exhibitions and programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another exciting development is also taking place at Kampong Java.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These venues that I have mentioned will offer our artists of various disciplines an affordable space to focus on their experimental and creative process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will seek views from the arts community on the use of these spaces in the first half of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our built heritage connects us to the nation's past, like what Mr Sitoh Yih Pin mentioned, and forms a part of our cultural identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin will be glad to know that MCCY is continuing to safeguard and celebrate Singapore's shared heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One important aspect of this work involves the heritage impact assessment (HIA) framework, which Minister for National Development Mr Desmond Lee had shared earlier at MND's COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY and NHB will continue to support MND and URA in implementing the HIA framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The framework further strengthens how public agencies must thoroughly evaluate the heritage significance of a site as an important consideration in the early stage of planning for development projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our rich heritage is also a source of national pride.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: All Singaporeans celebrated when our hawker culture was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in December 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, at the COS, I shared that we would embark on consultations to identify possible elements for Singapore's second UNESCO intangible cultural heritage nomination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Between June 2021 and January 2022, NHB held Focus Group Discussions with approximately 170 participants, comprising intangible cultural heritage practitioners, heritage business owners, academics and youths, to hear their views and their thoughts and suggestions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through these conversations, we heard a clear preference for our second nomination to be multicultural in nature and relatable to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, our Chingay Parade, the Making and Sharing of Kueh, Peranakan Beadwork and Embroidery, Orchid Cultivation and Yusheng, just to name a few.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NHB will broaden its consultations over the course of the coming months to engage more stakeholders, as well as the general public, before a final decision is made on the element to be nominated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Janet Ang spoke passionately about the importance of arts and culture for the young, and we agree with her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The CMSG will feature a range of topics, including Singapore's history and biodiversity, and help foster a stronger awareness of our shared values and national identity in our young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In another development, following extensive consultations with the community, the Peranakan Museum will reopen in 2023, with an expanded curatorial focus on the rich cross-cultural traditions and distinctive arts of the Peranakan communities in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides looking forward to the CMSG and Peranakan Museum, Singaporeans can all play a part in shaping an important reflection of our heritage – the Founders' Memorial.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Next month, NHB will launch the Founders' Memorial "Share Your Story, Shape Our Memorial" Travelling Exhibition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides an update on the Memorial's architectural design, the travelling exhibition will provide the public a chance to share artefacts and stories related to key national policies or milestones, or their encounters with our founding leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Mr Timothy de Souza is keen to share his personal mementoes as one of Singapore's first fighter pilots.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We look forward to rich and interesting contributions from all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin would be glad to know that, today, our arts sector includes diverse talents who collaborate and create new arts experiences for audiences in Singapore and beyond, including the under-reached groups mentioned by Ms Janet Ang and Mr Mark Chay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through signature arts festival platforms, such as SAW, which I mentioned earlier, Singapore International Festival of Arts and the Singapore Writers Festival, we have brought together diverse players in the local arts ecosystem, grown a strong audience base and profiled Singapore arts globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Community partnerships have been forged across 20 Arts and Culture nodes, bringing people of different backgrounds together through the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Arts education has also been enhanced with experiential, cohort-based learning programmes to museums and concert halls, as well as digital content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Arts offerings are more inclusive than before, with support for quality arts experiences for our preschoolers, as well as students with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will strengthen the role of the arts in the wider local and global creative economy; second, we will develop further ways for the arts to contribute to deepening our national identity, social cohesion and inclusivity; third, make the arts a distinctive factor that adds to Singapore's attractiveness as a global city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC welcomes feedback and ideas from the sector to refine Our SG Arts Plan 2.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our museums are now more accessible through digital initiatives and offerings that reach out to a larger audience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Seniors can now enjoy age-friendly programmes under the Silver Hubs initiative, while programmes under HeritageCares also reach out to lower-income families, persons with disabilities, children with special needs as well as youths-at-risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Heritage is being infused into everyday spaces around us through the Street Corner Heritage Galleries scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our Tampines Gallery, Kreta Ayer Heritage Gallery and Geylang Serai Heritage Gallery have all enlivened local communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We invite all Singaporeans to share your views and feedback for Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0 when NHB launches the public call in the middle of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Developing our local arts and heritage sectors enhances Singapore's vibrancy and attractiveness as a global city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Further, art pieces and heritage assets that resonate with Singaporeans will also strengthen our sense of belonging and help build a more cohesive and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY will strive to achieve these goals by continuing with our SG Arts and Heritage Plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since the launch of Our SG Arts Plan in 2018, we have profiled Singapore arts through signature arts platforms, forged community partnerships and brought arts across 20 arts and cultural nodes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This strengthens community involvement, including preschoolers, students with special needs and the elderly, ensuring that our arts scene becomes more inclusive and benefits more people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On the other hand, Our SG Heritage Plan, which was launched in 2018, has also allowed Singaporeans to rediscover and affirm their shared heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Preservation of more national monuments and the successful inscription of our hawker culture on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage have also engendered greater public recognition of the value of heritage in our everyday lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As the next step, NAC and NHB will broaden their consultations this year and continue their conversations with Singaporeans and partners from various fields as we co-create the next editions of Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans, so as to contribute to the creative economy and safeguard and promote Singapore's multicultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): Mdm Chairman, MCCY and our agencies remain committed to working with the arts and culture community to revitalise our arts and culture sector and chart its future directions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we build on the gains that we have made together over the past two years, we will carve an exciting journey ahead towards a thriving and sustainable arts and culture ecosystem – one that enriches livelihoods, unites our people and enlivens our city.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.45 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 5.24 pm until 5.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Chairman, many of us remember fondly the Kallang Roar, although I agree with Minister Edwin Tong when he said earlier that while it is great to revel in nostalgia, we should also look forward to the future of the bright talents that we have coming up through the Singapore football pipeline.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The project is a worthy one as it helps our youths undertake intensive and structured high-quality football training to play football professionally.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can MCCY provide an update on the progress of the Unleash the Roar project and its vision to unite Singaporeans of all ages, races and gender through football?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Chairman, soccer has always been a sport that unites our community since our national team participated in Malaysia Cup.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Aside from the Malaysia Cup matches back then, we used to host competitive international friendly tournaments, such as the Merlion Cup, which attracts participation from renowned international teams like South Korea and Saudi Arabia.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: At the last AFF Suzuki Cup between Singapore and Indonesia, where I was extremely fortunate to be physically inside the stadium with my family members and friends, we witnessed not just a match but a strong Singapore fighting spirit from our players, coupled with a multiracial crowd of all ages cheering the team on.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: The crowd support for the team on that night was one of passion and certainly brings back memories of the past glory days.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: In fact, the closure for that was when the crowd stood up and sang our national anthem to show appreciation for the players.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: They may have lost the match, but they have certainly reignited the spirit of the Kallang Roar.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Chairman, the last time our local soccer created a large interest in soccer was when we won the Malaysia Cup in 2015, even if the mood was less happening compared to 1994 when we won the Malaysian Cup League and Cup double.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Sadly, after every success in the Malaysia Cup for the last two occasions, we exited – either we exit by choice or Malaysia asked us to exit.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: How can we have more support for our local S League team, just like Lion City Sailors?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: I would also call on big organisations to play a pivotal role by being the main sponsor for all the S League clubs.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Only with good sponsorships can clubs bring in quality foreign players that complement our local players for more entertaining games that can also improve our local soccer standards.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: Singapore must develop more players with calibre of not just Quah Kim Song, but also like Harriss Harun, Faris Ramli, Jacob Mahler and Shahdan Sulaiman, for the future of our local soccer team that is not just of talent, but inclusive of all races that reflect Singapore as a multiracial society.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: We hope, by doing this, we do not just bring back the Kallang Roar, but we can even uplift the roar beyond Kallang and the Sports Hub!

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Although they were down to eight men, they put up a proud fight until the final whistle and could hold their heads up high despite the defeat.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The team's run in the tournament sparked a reinvigoration in local sentiments about our footballing scene.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Twelve years ago, another team bearing Singapore colours sparked the imagination of local football fans – the Singapore Youth Olympic Games (YOG) football team.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The players from that tournament were dubbed a "Golden Generation" not only for achieving a milestone bronze medal at the inaugural event, but also for their exciting style of play.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: And yet, a review of their fortunes a decade later told a story of a lost generation of footballers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: While it is true that youth footballing success is no guarantee of future achievement, we must also be mindful of other factors, such as failures in the training and development systems and the lack of quality in mentoring, coaching and grooming of young talents.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mark Chay, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Chairman, I would like to raise three points for MCCY to consider.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Two, additional resources to build our capabilities for sport science and administration.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: If not, what is the plan to ramp up in time for the games?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Many of our Team Singapore athletes are National Servicemen.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I would, therefore, like to ask if provisions have been made to enable and support our National Servicemen who have qualified for the games, for instance, allowing them time out to train and compete.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: At the outset, I would like to declare the I am a coach with the Singapore Disability Sports Council.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I will first speak on empowering coaches with the requisite knowledge and skills.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: As Singapore moves to be more inclusive in the sporting arena, it becomes all the more timely to ensure that coaches are equipped with the necessary skills to handle differently-abled athletes.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: On coaching education in the broader sense, I am happy to note that CoachSG is working with experts at Leeds Beckett University to develop a coaching competency framework that would impact and shape our coaching development and education pathway in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Chairman, I will move to my second point – recognising coaches and their accomplishments.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In my Budget 2022 Debate speech, I listed five Singaporean athletes who have emerged on top of the world in their respective disciplines.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Can we name all their coaches who helped them achieve this feat?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Do we know that these coaches were all local Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: And when was the last time we recognised a coach for a National Day Award?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The achievements of coaches have not enjoyed the same level of recognition as our national athletes do, and this should not be the case.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: They are with our athletes every step of the way, and these coaches not only ensure the physical performance of our athletes, they also play important roles in developing the athletes in imparting values and ethics.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I would, therefore, reason that their jobs are as important and deserving of recognition as those teachers at our MOE schools.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I now move to my final point – improving coaching standards and regulations.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: If we were to celebrate our coaches, we should also consider strengthening the regulatory framework which governs coaches, and sports for that matter.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The SafeSport Unified Code was launched last year and this was a huge step forward in ensuring the safety of our participants in sports.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: However, there is a lacuna in its ambit.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: What happens if the alleged offender is, for instance, an unregistered coach, a team manager or a volunteer?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: To plug this gap, I have two suggestions for the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I believe these measures would ensure a consistent standard and accountability for all persons who undertake the coaching role, which will then form a sturdy foundation for the sports scene in Singapore to thrive.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: Chairman, at first glance, sports and sustainability may seem to be two very different arenas.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: However, there may be opportunities for collaboration between the two sectors and communities for mutual benefit and the benefit of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
text: Could the Ministry share what additional initiatives are being considered to promote sustainability in sports?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, I would like to speak briefly about sports today – the role of sports in our lives and in our community.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I would like to start by recalling Minister Edwin Tong's response to one of my Parliamentary Questions recently.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In his response, the Minister laid out very comprehensively the overall framework – of our sporting system, sporting programmes and sporting infrastructure – and at various levels, from sports in the community, to sporting performance at the highest level.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And his response reminded me then that sports are a little bit like clean air in our lives; we tend to forget that it is there, until it is no longer there.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But I think, through years of effort, we have built up a framework that has allowed sports to become so integral a part of our lives and our community here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is in this spirit that I raise two questions, around what more we can do to strengthen the role of sports in our lives and our community.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Sports have the power to uplift and empower individuals.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It uplifts the spirit, it allows for the display and expression of talent and flair, it can help a person discover himself or herself.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: By extension, sports have the power to uplift and empower whole segments in society – more vulnerable children, youths at risk, persons with disabilities, seniors.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The Delta League by the Home Team is a good example.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: As Singaporeans, we cheer our national athletes on when they compete, we celebrate with them when they win and partake in their disappointment when they do not.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But, I think, we will reach the next level in our high-performance sporting culture here in Singapore when we can go beyond spectatorship, transcend spectatorship, to be an active part of the system and an active part of the movement.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In 2021, our para-athletes shone on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For the 2020 Summer Paralympics in Tokyo, Team Singapore fielded 10 athletes across six sports to compete with the world's best and represent Singapore at the highest sporting showcase.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In October last year, this House resolved in a Motion to congratulate Team Singapore Olympians and Paralympians for their achievements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our para-athletes have been an inspiration to us all.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They show us what it means to defy the odds and what is possible when you are not defined or constrained by physical limitations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We can, and should, draw from their example to encourage more participation in sports in Singapore, especially among persons with disabilities (PWDs).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For one, sports activities are a good way to keep healthy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We heard yesterday at the MOH COS debate about preventive health, and physical activity is an important component of a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Sports activities not only help with physical wellness, but also mental well-being as participants interact with others and build relationships through their interactions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With facilitation and proper guidance, PWDs can acquire useful social skills and build up their confidence as they participate in sports activities that they enjoy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Thirdly, there is so much potential to promote inclusiveness through sports.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Sports are a social leveller that does not distinguish between educational levels, socio-economic status, race or religion.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It helps bring together people from all walks of life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We can support and cheer for one another and use common facilities together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This would help normalise different abilities and open doors to a better appreciation and understanding of differences.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are inclusive gyms and several disability sports programmes and also efforts by SportSG.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I also understand that various stakeholders like Singapore Disability Sports Council and MOE, work with SportSG to enable talent development in disability sports and strengthen capabilities in the ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Have there been developments on inclusive physical exercise and disability sports programmes?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Are knowledge and expertise in tailoring sports activities for PWDs and organising inclusive sports programmes sufficiently widespread?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I hope the Ministry can share its plans to leverage sports to make Singapore a more inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has brought about much disruption and challenges to all, including our youths.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our young people had to contend with significant changes in their educational journey and there was a particularly specific impact for those who were in certain courses of study or at the tail end of their formal education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They had to quickly adjust to learning online, with less interaction with teachers and other students.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It was especially challenging for those in technical courses where hands-on learning is important.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Internship programmes had to be adjusted as firms implemented work-from-home arrangements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Those who had planned to study overseas or go for an exchange programme had their plans disrupted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Prospects for some industries appeared bleak as the economy pivoted and some wondered about their choice of study and career prospects.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some young people I spoke to expressed how the pandemic has robbed them of their opportunities and youth.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The impact on their mental well-being was, indeed, significant.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: According to the NYC Youth Statistics in Brief 2020, the youth labour force participation rates for the year 2019 was 61% for ages 20 to 24; 90.1% for ages 25 to 29; 92.3% for ages 30 to 34.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: According to the MOM report in June 2021, the youth unemployment rate climbed in 2020.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While the situation is challenging for those transiting from school to work, I feel that our youths have shown a lot of resilience in overcoming their situation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There may be industries affected, but there are many opportunities and new growth areas.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is important, therefore, to strategically look at how we can support our youths to seize the opportunities and provide them with the relevant insights, so that they are motivated and have the necessary information to make decisions for their future.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I do not think I need to extol the virtues of mentoring to this House.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We all know the value of having that someone in your life to give guidance and motivation as you venture into new unknown and challenging areas.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would like though to emphasise the importance of mentoring in opening world views and nudging young people to explore possibilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is especially significant for families of certain economic status, where their children do not benefit from the social capital of those who are more well-to-do or well-connected.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Their world view may be circumscribed by what they see their parents do.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Even if they get inspired by someone they read or hear about in the news, they do not know how to get there, how to achieve the same things.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Further, not everyone is as fortunate to meet a mentor who can guide her along.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to make sure that every young person has access to the support she needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That way, every young person will have access to mentors and, when they grow older, may be mentors themselves.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There is a lot of awareness now about mental well-being and its impact on the holistic development of an individual.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I believe with these efforts, we can continue to encourage our youths to be resilient and hopeful for the future.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Hany Soh, you can take both cuts, please.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In my previous green, sustainability-related Parliamentary speeches, I have shared my firm belief that community involvement plays a vital role in our overall nation's efforts towards SG Green Plan 2030 through our collective efforts and embracing an eco-friendly lifestyle and greenify the environment.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In order to achieve that, the Government needs to set up the right hardware and co-create the green software.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Active SG Woodlands Sports Centre situated in our Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC is one such example.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A community farm was actually set up right next to its swimming pool and is being cared for by a team of passionate Team Nila Volunteers, as well as members of the public living around the vicinity of Marsiling and Woodgrove.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The ground-up recycling effort at this community farm is commendable.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Most of the fittings there are actually recycled items contributed and creatively put together by residents and ActiveSG staff.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They have also exhibited their innovativeness by harvesting rainwater to irrigate the greens.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These green farming activities not only keep the members active and fit but also build a strong kampong spirit as they routinely contribute the harvest to the vulnerable groups in our community, along with sharing their green tips to other community gardens within the neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Minister Edwin Tong has previously shared his views that our young people are a crucial segment of our society.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The youths of today are the leaders of tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our youths are the people who must have a say in the kind of society they want to be in and should play an active role in shaping Singapore's future.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Youths today, however, faced many uncertainties, magnified by the COVID-19 pandemic and other global issues.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of them are also in transition through different life stages.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These have placed a significant amount of stress on our young people, especially in areas, such as job prospects, finances and mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Despite these challenges, we have witnessed many of them tirelessly volunteering their time and effort in serving the vulnerable groups in our community during this eventful period.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am particularly grateful to the youths in our Woodgrove community.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Despite facing their own challenges, they have organised mental wellness talks to motivate others to stay positive, distributed "Return to School" care packs to low-income group children, hosted upcycling "Go Green" workshops and planned many clean-up estate initiatives to raise empathy for our cleaners.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How does the whole Government intend to work together to support youths in navigating their various life stages and transitions?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has also been done to provide opportunities and support to our youths of different cultures and backgrounds to continue contributing to the community and mold the future of our Singapore, despite the present challenges that each of them may be facing now?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: He was a good boy who was always giving, always there to support his peers, to counsel and encourage them to not take their lives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: He studied in an Arts school and did not take a conventional path.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I saw him not too long before he took his life, as I had only just given out an Edusave award to his sibling.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I was at his wake, saw his mother and spoke with his friends who all missed him very dearly.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: So, youths today face many uncertainties and pressures – ranging from body image to grades, to relationships and to whether they have a future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Many youths are also in transition through different life stages.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Arguably, if even adults having a few hard knocks in life already struggle when hit with a crisis, what more for youths?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Mental well-being has now come to the fore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It used to be a topic brushed away and shunned by many.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I spoke on this for years in Parliament and when I was an undergraduate.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But now, we are forced to come face-to-face with it as we endure the pandemic but, thankfully, there is now a general public will to address it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I know stress is not something one can legislate away.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But the Government can direct resources through the right channels in a timely manner to help our youths through difficult times, to help build their resilience.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Some of the stress could be mitigated by guiding them in the right direction, such as proactive career counselling and matching, and timely intervention to stop physical or online bullying.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But, often times, it is also about letting them know that they are not alone, that there is someone or groups of people whom they can turn to for a listening ear, for positive affirmation, for advice and to nudge them to embrace a growth mindset.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: That someone may not always be a family member and that is okay.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How will the whole-of-Government, therefore, work together to be present in their lives, to give and show support to our youths as they transition from one stage to the next?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Edwin Tong spoke about our transition out of the pandemic – to build towards a strong, caring and inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our national monuments embody our foundational values and where we come from.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Elgin Bridge, located just next to this House, is one of them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It quietly symbolises our openness to the world, our strength in diversity, our adaptability for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It symbolically connected Singapore and the world, through facilitating trade for our city's growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It connected the culturally different towns of our Indian and Chinese migrants living on South Bridge Road, to the Malay and European community living across on North Bridge Road.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Elgin Bridge that we walk on today is a result of four major reconstructions over two centuries, adapting to the times of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Elgin Bridge continues to bear witness to our Singapore story – where we build connections with the world, re-invent ourselves for the future, bridge our differences and forge a shared identity amid our diversity.
