speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I will first touch on our youths, who will realise our future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Together with them, we will continue to build bridges to the world, towards our shared future vision of Singapore and with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I chat regularly with our youths, and two issues that they deeply care about are the future of work and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked how we can better support our youths, especially in their jobs, finances and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths know they need to prepare themselves for their future careers and desire three things: (a) opportunities to learn, (b) concrete skills to offer, and (c) guidance along the way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we are building bridges to our region and beyond, to help them to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, we are building bridges all the way with Latin America – a region with immense growth potential, to help Singapore startups enter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths who are setting their sights beyond Singapore can, therefore, look forward to more global opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: During the Budget Debates, Mr Desmond Choo referred to our youths as "Generation COVID-19" – coming-of-age during the pandemic, in an era of many opportunities, but also, unique challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths need the confidence to seize opportunities by acquiring concrete skills and knowledge, and we have developed three initiatives on this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, our Asia-Ready Exposure Programme (AEP) helps bridge our youths to the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through online content and physical trips when possible, we are developing our youths' cross-cultural skills for opportunities in Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our AEP recently collaborated with the Ministry of Trade and Industry Academy on a webinar programme titled "Regional Economies and Trade", to equip our youths with insights on market economies, like ASEAN, China and India.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths learnt first-hand from industry leaders in Asia, from companies like Quest Ventures, a top VC fund in Asia; YCH Group, a leading regional supply chain management partner; and Riverwalk Holdings, an India-focused VC fund, on what it is like to work abroad and what skills you need to succeed in the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we are creating opportunities to bridge our youths to local organisations, in the community and social sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will build on this as we recover from the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through the Youth Corps Community Internship (YCCI), MCCY and NYC will partner social and community organisations to offer internships, with priority given to ITE and the Polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths can pick up skills like event and project management, marketing and community engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, we will build and strengthen bridges for our youths, with mentors, as they navigate life's many milestones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Rahayu Mahzam's question about mentoring opportunities to support our youths emotionally is thus key.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, to any youth looking for a mentor, the Mentoring AfA has established WeConnect, Singapore's first dedicated online mentoring platform, where you can find programmes, ranging from mentoring opportunities to community groups, for your personal life-stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: You can learn from mentors who have traversed career journeys across industries like tech, logistics, media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: By the end of this month, you can register on WeConnect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And I highly encourage you to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how we are supporting youths struggling with mental health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: During the Budget debates, Dr Shahira Abdullah and Ms Nadia Samdin stressed the importance of stronger mental health support in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Even as the pandemic wanes, mental health issues will not just disappear with it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We need to reinforce support for our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We want our youths to know that it is okay to reach out and share about their mental health and well-being without fear of judgement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To build supportive communities, we will expand peer support networks across various settings, be it in schools, workplaces, online and in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY and NYC are partnering our Youth Sector Organisations, like Campus Psy and Young NTUC, to run peer support network programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also encouraging trained peer supporters from ITE, Polytechnics and Universities to continue serving the community after graduation, by joining our Youth Corps Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And our youths are leading the way on mental health awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Happiness Initiative, Calm Collective and Limitless, are just three of the many ground-up initiatives they are spearheading.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And to bring together these efforts, the Government started our Youth Mental Well-being Network (YMWBN) in 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But mental health issues do not only affect our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, to achieve even greater impact, we will expand the efforts of the YMWBN to a broader network, which will tackle mental health issues across a broader range of population segments, as mentioned by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary in his speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This wider network will be a platform for those who can deliver mental health and well-being outcomes, like Campus Psy and Calm Collective, to come together and spearhead initiatives, with funding support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For those who would benefit from these initiatives, the Network could help you find useful services and initiatives more easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, whether you are an organisation, a student, a middle-age PMET, or senior looking for mental well-being support, we welcome you to be part of this effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY will support this network, which will be advised by the Interagency Taskforce for Mental Health and Well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I feel privileged to chair this network with the support of my colleagues Minister of State Sun Xueling and Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will announce more details later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have learnt a lot from the YMWBN and we will build upon the learnings and networks to build a more inclusive Singapore that prioritises our mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next, we must look ahead, or construct new bridges to our desired future, with our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At MCCY, we have already begun the work and are now seeing the early fruits of our labour through the Youth Action Challenge (YAC) and the Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through the YAC, any youth with an idea and a desire to tackle the problems of our day, can pitch their innovative project idea and receive grants to realise these solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Many of their projects have made tangible impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Take, for example, the team Skilio, founded by our youths Felix, Dody and Zhi Hui, with a simple but ambitious vision: creating a society where we are recognised for our unique strengths – not defined by the schools we go to, or the letters on our report cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Skilio puts these ideals into a tangible product – a digital portfolio that helps youths document any soft skills picked up along their educational journey, to pursue their dream careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This reflects how our youths' ideas can and have made an impact, and, indeed, a difference to many.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also offering our youths a dedicated physical space to prototype their ideas and implement ground-up programmes for social causes through our Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since 2019, Somerset Belt has supported more than 20 ground-up projects, reaching more than 20,000 youths on causes like arts, environment and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the year ahead, we will partner institutes like Singapore Polytechnic and Singapore University of Technology and Design to translate ideas from classrooms and studios into real life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also refresh and enhance the spaces within Somerset Belt in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Thus far, we have sought ideas from over 240 youths on how they envision or want to use this space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Some envision the Belt to be a Creative Hub, with experimental retail spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue to grow and make our youth-initiated ideas come alive through funding support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will announce more details on the refresh works on the Somerset Belt later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, we have already seen early fruits from the YAC and the Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In time, especially with the upcoming YAC Season 4 starting October, we will see even more youths coming forward to make their impact, and, in fact, I welcome youths to come and join our YAC Season 4.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to speak in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In Mandarin):   Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about other plans for youths to take action on social causes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will match our youths to neighbours in need, to support underprivileged families, senior citizens and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In English): I will next talk about building our youths' civic capacity for constructive discourse with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, with tech and social media as the frontiers for social discourse, we need to strengthen mutual understanding, especially on key and contentious societal issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While we see more open discussions on social media, we also see growing polarisation, echo chambers and the rise of cancel culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When I spoke with youths at the launch of the Inter-University Network last month, they shared with me their wish to discuss difficult and controversial issues frankly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They want to work with us to build what they call safe spaces and also guardrails to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why Prof Koh Lian Pin's question about opportunities for youth participation on topics of national interest is key, relevant and timely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will work with our youths to create safe platforms for them to explore and engage in a diversity of views and help them build empathy towards those who hold different views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will address key topics like race and religion, local-foreigner relations and intergenerational bonding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths can participate in a variety of online platforms like Instagram Live! sessions with expert panels and access the content through a microsite.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will pick up useful tips on how to engage in difficult conversations and converse constructively on complex issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, we must consciously strengthen the bridges that connect us, not just across the diversity of our perspectives but also across our different racial, religious and ethnic backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman asked about our integration efforts to build a cohesive society and bridge societal fault lines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In addition to the work of our Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) as covered by Minister Edwin Tong, our National Integration Council and Singapore Citizenship Journey are important platforms for this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Both platforms help us to strengthen the bridges between locals and newcomers to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We must never forget that Singapore's story has always been one of an immigrant nation embracing diversity and being open to the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As part of our Emerging Stronger Conversations, members of the National Integration Council (NIC) candidly discussed challenges around local-foreigner relations, particularly arising from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We developed three key themes that the NIC's Alliance for Action and its projects will focus on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, to create more shared experiences and interactions through a community orientation programme and volunteering opportunities where newcomers and locals can have meaningful interactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, to share positive stories that inspire us to embrace the vibrancy of our diverse backgrounds and common aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Third, to empower and equip more to speak up on sensitive issues relating to diversity and inclusion by developing workshops and programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Everyone can play a part in this effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The efforts of the IRCCs and the NIC emphasise our shared Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But what does it mean to be Singaporean and to live in Singapore?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through our Citizens' Workgroup for Singapore Citizenship Journey (SCJ) in 2020, Singaporeans answered this question.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They reflected that it is our shared languages and experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is how we order kopi with our uniquely Singaporean language, whether it is "kopi-o" or "kopi-c" or "kopi peng".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is our community spirit and shared values where we believe it is our responsibility to care for one another and to leave no one behind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Thanks to our citizens' contributions, we have included refreshed content in our e-Journey and new e-Book, such as our arts and culture and aspirations for Singapore's future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: You can experience the e-Journey now through the Singapore Journey website and look forward to the launch of the e-Book next month, titled "Welcome to Singapore".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I hope these resources remind us about the heart of being a Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, our IRCCs, NIC and SCJ strengthen the ties between our different ethnic and religious communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The solidarity they foster is our nation's source of strength, which we must not take for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Walking across Elgin Bridge towards South Bridge Road, we can see how our diversity exists in harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Along this one road, we have the Masjid Jamae Chulia, Sri Mariamman Temple, the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple and the Fairfield Methodist Church.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is the diversity that our forefathers built our nation on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: By building stronger bridges across communities, our diversity will continue to be our defining strength.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, Minister Edwin Tong reminded us that our transition out of the pandemic will not be without obstacles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, COVID-19 has changed the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These past two-plus years, we have had to fight the pandemic together, yet acutely apart.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But like other crises we have weathered before, we can overcome COVID-19.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But to do so, we must strengthen the sense of "us".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I will now outline how MCCY will build a more caring, inclusive and united society through volunteerism and sports.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Prof Koh Lian Pin asked about efforts to build a more sustainable sports ecosystem.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, we are partnering the sports industry to reduce, recondition and recycle sports equipment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, we will rally our National Sports Associations (NSAs), Team Nila volunteers and ActiveSG Sport Centres to amplify our sustainability efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have brought community gardens like the one Ms Hany Soh described to other ActiveSG Sport Centres to cultivate community ties through green initiatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about opportunities for Singaporeans to volunteer and to care for others.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through the SG Cares movement, MCCY will work with community partners to make volunteerism our way of life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, SG Cares is partnering professional bodies, such as the Law Society Pro Bono Services, to champion skills-based volunteerism.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We aim to grow regular volunteers and deepen our culture of care and service to the community within these professional bodies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, in every town, the SG Cares Volunteer Centres (VCs) and SG Cares Community Networks are fostering collaborations with partners, such as schools, corporates, ground-up movements and Social Service Agencies (SSAs), to channel volunteers to areas of need.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, we will continue to enhance our charities' capabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Charities and Institutions of a Public Character will continue to receive funding support to strengthen their governance and management capabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lastly, we have made volunteering even more accessible through the SSAs and SG Cares VCs, which have pivoted to virtual volunteering opportunities, such as online storytelling and exercise sessions, that engage diverse age groups.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan rightly pointed out that sports have the power to uplift underserved communities and change lives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Indeed, sports are a powerful force for good and a great social leveller.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG's SportCares will partner MSF's ComLink to offer programmes like its flagship "Saturday Night Lights", a structured football programme, to families with children and youths living in rental housing.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will be launched to all 21 ComLink towns, but starting with five this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope to reach out to 28,000 children and youths across about 300 public rental housing blocks by 2027.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sports also play a critical developmental role for youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It shapes character, teaches resilience and teamwork and builds communities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Having mentored ITE students myself for many years, I strongly believe that every youth has potential, regardless of what their starting point in life is.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In addition to WeConnect that Minister of State Alvin Tan mentioned earlier, SportCares has launched a mentoring programme to support 100 disadvantaged young people over the next two years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, we will support our youths through internships, scholarships and bursaries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From July, SportCares will offer industry attachments within SportSG and industry partners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportCares has also committed $400,000 towards the SportCares Scholarship.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Up to 20 SportCares youths will be supported to pursue either a NITEC, tertiary or undergraduate course in a locally recognised institution.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Up to 1,400 children, youths and persons with disabilities (PwDs) from low-income backgrounds will benefit from the SportCares Bursary Scheme, which covers the fees to any ActiveSG Academies and Clubs programme for at least a season of 10 weeks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Darryl David, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about efforts to provide more inclusive opportunities through sports.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In my MSF speech earlier, I spoke about the Enabling Masterplan 2030 and our whole-of-society efforts to make Singapore more inclusive.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To that end, disability sports play an important role.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since the launch of the Disability Sports Masterplan (DSMP) in 2016, we have made good progress.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We widened the base of disability sports participation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will make our sports facilities more accessible and will make all ActiveSG Gyms inclusive by 2026.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also promoted inclusion through sharing sporting experiences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay raised the importance of empowering coaches to better support PwDs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked if expertise in this area is sufficiently widespread.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, CoachSG runs curated coaching courses under the Special Olympics Singapore and Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: About 2,800 coaches, educators, volunteers, staff and students have been trained in inclusive sports programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To equip more coaches with disability sports coaching competencies, CoachSG will incorporate this into the National Registry of Coaches' (NROC) SG-Coach Level Two curriculum this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Para Sport Academy will drive the integration of disability and mainstream sports in our ActiveSG Academies and Clubs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They will also provide aspiring para-athletes a clear pathway from recreational participation to high-performance sports.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope that the Para Sport Academy will be an enabling platform through which more persons with disabilities can build their self-confidence and reach their fullest potential.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is also our ambition to grow a new generation of para-athletes who will go on to represent Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To better ensure that the Para Sport Academy serves the needs of para-athletes, SportSG has established an advisory panel comprising prominent members of the disability sports community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With their extensive experience in and contributions to para sports, the panel will be well-placed to co-design and grow the Para Sport Academy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay spoke about raising coaching standards and recognising coaches.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On raising coaching standards and regulations, SportSG is working on creating a larger national registry to include coaches and fitness instructors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under the Safe Coach Programme that is being rolled out, all sports participants in member organisations, including administrators and volunteers will be bound by the Safe Sport Unified Code.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay also asked about the Coaching Competency Framework that CoachSG is developing with Leeds Beckett University.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will inform our formal coach education curriculum.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When recognised as part of the sport sector Industry Transformation Map, coaches can use the framework to compare the competencies and remuneration of coaching against jobs in adjacent sectors, thereby promoting greater occupational mobility.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With established recommended rates, coaches will be remunerated fairly and it is our hope that the coaching profession will become more attractive.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On recognising our coaches, today there are various awards, such as the Coach of the Year Award by the Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) and SDSC, as well as CoachSG's Singapore Coach Medallion.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, 2022 will be yet another busy year for our Team Singapore athletes, as they represent Singapore at the Hanoi SEA Games, the Birmingham Commonwealth Games, the Surakarta ASEAN Para Games and the Hangzhou Asian and Asian Para Games.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Keeping in top form will be of utmost importance and Mr Mark Chay will be reassured to know that we are supporting our athletes as best as we can.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our support for national athletes is comprehensive and takes both financial and non-financial forms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Funding support for major games is also planned in advance and accounted for within the NSA's multi-year sports plan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also continually invest resources to enhance the Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) and the National Youth Sport Institute (NYSI).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, both have quality infrastructure to provide sports science and medicine support to our national athletes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Whether it is access to funding, sports science or medicine, the support rendered to each athlete is customised based on individual needs, and specific demands of their sport.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On National Service, the priority of full-time National Servicemen is their military duties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are working with MINDEF to support our Team Singapore athletes to address their sports training needs while fulfilling military duties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Provisions like short-term deferment, leave and time-off to train and compete are available, subject to the SAF's operational needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Corporates and Singaporeans can also contribute to our athletes' journeys.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the One Team Singapore Fund (OTSF) and efforts to encourage a spirit of giving to sports.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Darryl David asked about efforts to rally Singaporeans to support Team Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The OTSF offers one-to-one matching for donations and has matched almost $15 million since its inception in 2017.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Your donations and matching grant will benefit our athletes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also establish Team Singapore Cares, a platform for Team Singapore athletes to serve and give back.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Team Singapore athletes will be able to tap on the Active Citizen Grant to spearhead initiatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG will also support them to connect them with Corporate Partners who can help to co-fund these projects.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Allow me to provide an update on the progress on "Unleash the Roar!", our national project to uplift Singapore football.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This year, we started 10 School Football Academies (SFAs) in secondary schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We want to provide a nurturing environment for students to hone their football skills while supporting them academically.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Almost 400 students have enrolled in our SFAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our ambition is to grow them to full capacity over the next few years with a total of 16 SFAs for boys across all secondary levels.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we also plan to establish SFAs for girls as well.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A key factor in the SFAs' success is quality coaching.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To give our students the best training environment, each SFA will feature a dedicated Head Coach, assistant coaches and zonal specialist coaches.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Five have started coaching since mid-January, and we will onboard 12 more by April.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond youth and coach development, we will set into motion other plans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The scholarship will provide financial support to talented and committed footballers to immerse themselves in a high-performance football environment abroad while pursuing their studies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also plan to support more young talents to go overseas on stints to broaden their exposure.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, we will do more for women's football here in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will grow the participation base by introducing more programmes for girls under the ActiveSG Football Academy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will provide our women footballers greater support by way of training facilities, coaching and sports science.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, beyond the resumption of the Singapore Premier League (SPL), MCCY and SportSG have been working with partners, such as the Football Association of Singapore (FAS), on opportunities for our football teams to compete with international teams on home ground.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Singaporeans can look forward to supporting the Lions at the upcoming football triangular series against the Philippines and Malaysia.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am sure some Members of the House also fondly recall the Lion City Cup.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Pandemic restrictions aside, we hope to bring our young competitors from the region into Singapore, so that our youths can compete at a high level and, at the same time, generate excitement about youth football.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We look forward to sharing more when these plans are firmed up.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about the replacement of our national coach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I understand the FAS' recruitment process for this position has been set in motion and we will be hearing from them in due course.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many have asked me how I felt, leading the charge on this front.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I would be lying if I said I do not have butterflies in my stomach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because of the many passionate individuals I had spent hours talking to about this project.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And because of our Lions, the way they fought their Indonesian rivals at the Suzuki Cup semi-finals last year on Christmas Day!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And most of all, because of how Singaporeans reacted to them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: What we witnessed that night has got to be one of the most, if not the most gripping, Singapore football performance in recent history.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And the immense sense of pride that we felt when Majulah Singapura filled the National Stadium – never mind that there were only 10,000 of us that evening!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That, Members of this Chamber, is the power of sports, the power of football, and that is why we must believe in Singapore football and we must believe that we can Unleash the Roar!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Across our different sectors – community, arts, sports, youth – we all have a role to play in shaping a Singapore that is caring, cohesive and confident.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is our strength in unity and collective fortitude that will enable us to overcome the pandemic and build a brighter tomorrow, and a stronger Singapore Together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: This clarification is in relation to Youth Corp Community Internship (YCCI), which Minister of State Alvin Tan had shared with us earlier on the internship opportunities for youths in the social and community sectors in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I wish to enquire whether we can consider extending it to overseas opportunities in this aspect as well.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: One example is the youth exchange programme organised previously by the Central CDC under its High 5 Youth initiative many years ago, which I personally benefited as a student leader.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Awardees participate in the exchange programme in countries, such as Australia and Xiamen, China, to better understand the local community's good practices on matters, such as intergenerational bonding, and put them into practice when they return to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But I wanted to let the Member know that we have other programmes and one of the most appropriate ones is called the Youth Expedition Project (YEP), which is run by Youth Corp Singapore for youths to, in fact, do what exactly the Member mentioned – to serve other communities overseas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The YEP programme usually spans about four to six months if you factor in preparation, planning as well as post-trip reflections.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have it online now; so, it is YEP Go Online.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is not as ideal as we would love to, because nothing beats being there physically, but we plan to restart it very soon, hopefully, when travel resumes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we have these programmes in place and we hope to restart these programmes when travel resumes.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I would just like to make two clarifications.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: One is to ask the Minister about the establishment of gaming, digital content and technology hub and the second is on the Para Sports Academy.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: And what are the tangible goals to understand what the success of this Para Sports Academy will look like?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To deal with his first point, Mr Chay might be pleased to know that we have been working with partners, such as the Global Sport Innovation Centre (GSIC), and just a few months back in December last year, GSIC launched the Asia Pacific HQ in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having partners like GSIC in Singapore means that we will aggregate the thought leadership in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As Members know, with gaming, technology and innovation, there is a natural synergy, a confluence of various aspects of this gaming and fitness industry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we will have a place in Singapore where we will have content and game developers coalesce, we will have hardware developers as well, and, of course, those who are involved in technology, including things like wearables, which are gaining prevalence in the way in which we do fitness.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, all of that will be in Singapore and we intend to work with them to develop this ecosystem and strengthen Singapore's position for sport-tech solutions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In relation to the para sports academies, we intend to work with several sports first, as a start.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the first instance, we will probably use the existing framework and infrastructure and work with the Disabilities Sports Council to see how we can move the para-athletes into the system in this way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think that is the fastest way to scale up.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over time, I appreciate that each sport may be different and the way in which we train, nurture and develop our para-athletes may be different sport to sport, and may also be different between a para-athlete and an able-bodied athlete.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, as we develop the base and infrastructure, we will begin to scale up with the expertise so that more of them can enter the system in this way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If the able-bodied athletes have a certain pathway opportunity, we intend to make sure that we put the para-athletes on the same track, on the same path, so that there is equality, if not in terms of outcomes, certainly, in terms of where the starting point should be.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It is very heartening to hear the plans shared by Minister of State Low Yen Ling and Minister Edwin Tong about how they intend to support, invigorate and promote the arts industry in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Minister Edwin Tong talked about having safe spaces for the arts, for expression and development.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I would just like to ask the Minister if he could perhaps expound a bit more on whether there will be more of such spaces that will be provided for our arts community and also what are some of the resources and facilities that could perhaps be put in place in these spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When it comes to arts spaces, our objective is really, one.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In some cases, we update the spaces, so that old spaces can be used for new purposes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over time, I think we have had the opportunity to grow the spaces available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we continually look at how we can refresh the existing spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will just give you some examples, some of which my colleagues have touched on earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We all know that it used to be a place where container cranes and so on occupy those spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But if you think about it, it is actually quite intuitive to use it as an arts space – high ceilings, large walls – you can have displays there that you cannot otherwise do in our current settings or spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we are using this as an experiment to develop this into a new hub for arts spaces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member spoke about 45 Armenian Street as well – 45 Armenian Street is a place with lots of history.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many of our arts practitioners know the place as a young experimental place with buzz where you come in, you incubate, you spend some time learning from each other as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we wanted to develop this with the same kind of feeling and ethos.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it is in that respect that we invited practitioners, leaders of the arts community – Mae Anderson, Janice Koh, and I mentioned some names earlier – to come and share their experience with us and think in terms of how to envision this space for future use.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Kampong Java is another space that we looked at.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of you probably drive past it each day and not realise that it is there.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It used to be used terrace houses that are now disused.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we worked with SLA to take advantage of the fact that it has not been used and see how we could repurpose it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we are working with the arts industry also to get ideas as to how this can be managed and operated.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Is the hon Member given leave to withdraw his amendment?
